faqs.question: What are 10 easy lines on Diwali for nursery kids?
faqs.answer: Use lines of three to five words a child can say in one breath, such as "We light little lamps" and "Diwali is a happy festival." At ages 3 to 5, NCERT's 2022 foundational framework treats drawing and scribbling as early writing, so these lines are for saying aloud, not writing.

faqs.question: Can my child copy these lines for school homework?
faqs.answer: Use them as models to read and learn from, not to hand in word for word. A child learns more by swapping one real detail from their own Diwali into each line, and teachers can usually spot copied lines.

faqs.question: When is Diwali in 2027?
faqs.answer: Diwali 2027 (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Friday, 29 October, per Drik Panchang. The five days run from Dhanteras on 27 October to Bhai Dooj on 31 October 2027, and Diwali 2026 is on Sunday, 8 November.

faqs.question: What is the main reason Diwali is celebrated?
faqs.answer: Many North Indian families celebrate Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after fourteen years in the forest, while parts of South India mark Lord Krishna's victory over Narakasura. Lakshmi Puja on the new-moon night honours Goddess Lakshmi, and in West Bengal many families worship Goddess Kali at this time.

faqs.question: How many sentences can a Class 3 child write about Diwali?
faqs.answer: NCERT's 2017 learning outcomes expect a Class 3 child to write 5–6 sentences on personal experiences, so ten lines is a stretch at that age. Let the child write six from their own Diwali and borrow four from a model set.

faqs.question: Should a Class 2 child's Diwali lines include a date?
faqs.answer: One date is enough at that age, for example "In 2027, Diwali falls on Friday, 29 October." It shows the child that some lines are facts that can be checked, while the rest describe their own family.

faqs.question: Is it okay to mention firecrackers in 10 lines on Diwali?
faqs.answer: It is fine to mention them, but many schools now ask pupils to celebrate with diyas and rangoli instead of loud crackers. A safety line, such as keeping a bucket of water near the lamps, usually reads better to a teacher.

faqs.question: What Diwali words can UKG children trace?
faqs.answer: Short words work best: "lamp", "oil", "dots", "box", "pray" and "glow". NCERT's 2017 outcomes expect Class 1 children to write simple words like "fan" and "hen", so UKG tracing builds toward that.

faqs.question: Why does Diwali fall on a different date every year?
faqs.answer: Diwali follows the Hindu lunar calendar and falls on the new-moon night (Amavasya), so its Gregorian date shifts each year. In 2027 the Amavasya tithi ends at 7:05 pm on 29 October in New Delhi, per Drik Panchang.

faqs.question: Can my child send their Diwali lines to grandparents online?
faqs.answer: Yes. On SubhSandesh's Diwali card, a parent can type a few of the child's lines as diya wishes and add up to six photos, and the private link opens in any browser with no app. For homework, keep the handwritten version, because the page is a greeting, not an essay.

article.contentMarkdown:
# 10 Lines on Diwali for Every Class, Nursery to Class 5

Here are seven original sets of 10 lines on Diwali, one each for nursery and LKG, UKG and Classes 1 to 5, with lines growing from about 5 words to about 14. Every date is checked: Diwali 2027 (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Friday, 29 October, and Diwali 2026 on Sunday, 8 November.

SubhSandesh makes Diwali greeting pages, not homework, and two platform numbers shaped the last section: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, and a page is viewed 11.1 times on average (both measured September 2026). Below are the sets, a table against NCERT's class goals, and how to make the lines the child's own.

## How long should 10 lines on Diwali be for each class?

Ten lines on Diwali is a school task: ten separate sentences about the festival, one idea per line. NCERT's [Learning Outcomes at the Elementary Stage (April 2017)](https://ncert.nic.in/pdf/publication/otherpublications/tilops101.pdf) expects a Class 1 child to write simple words like "fan" and "hen", a Class 3 child to write 5–6 sentences about personal experiences, and a Class 5 child to write paragraphs joined by linkers.

So younger children say or copy their sets. The [National Curriculum Framework for the Foundational Stage (NCERT, October 2022)](https://ncert.nic.in/pdf/NCF_for_Foundational_Stage_20_October_2022.pdf) counts scribbling as early writing, and spellings like "kat" for "cat" as a normal step.

## Seven original sets of 10 lines on Diwali, nursery to Class 5

Each set gives the ages, average words per line and one new skill. Every line is original to this page.

### 1. Nursery and LKG (ages 3–5): about 5 words a line, to say aloud

These are for reciting, or saying under a drawing. The skill is speaking a full sentence.

- Diwali is a happy festival.
- We light little lamps.
- The lamps are called diyas.
- Our home looks so bright.
- Mumma makes a pretty rangoli.
- I wear my new clothes.
- We eat sweet laddoos.
- We pray to Goddess Lakshmi.
- I hug my grandma tight.
- Happy Diwali to everyone!

### 2. UKG (ages 5–6): about 6 words a line, with words to trace

Words like "oil" and "box" are easy to trace. The skill is copying a sentence with a capital and a full stop.

- Diwali is the festival of lamps.
- It comes in October or November.
- Papa and I dust every shelf.
- I help fill the diyas with oil.
- Nana hangs marigolds on the door.
- My sister makes a rangoli with dots.
- In the evening, we all pray.
- We open a big box of sweets.
- The whole street glows with lights.
- I love Diwali with my family.

### 3. Class 1 (ages 6–7): about 8 words a line, one detail each

Each line adds one detail: a food, a colour or a person. NCERT's Class 1 goal is single words, so copying is enough.

- Diwali is a big festival of India.
- People light clay lamps and fairy lights.
- There is no moon in the sky that night.
- We keep a small Lakshmi idol near the lamps.
- My mother makes kheer and hot puris.
- I wear a yellow kurta in the evening.
- We take sweets to the guard uncle at our gate.
- My friends and I make a paper lantern.
- Our rangoli has red, green and orange colours.
- Diwali makes everyone smile.

### 4. Class 2 (ages 7–8): about 10 words a line, with the first real date

This set adds the 2027 date and the Ramayana story. A Grade 2 teacher's note in NCERT's 2022 framework names pronouns as a next step; lines 4 and 5 practise them.

- Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, celebrated across India.
- In 2027, Diwali falls on Friday, 29 October.
- Many families tell the story of Lord Rama coming home to Ayodhya.
- He had lived in the forest for fourteen years.
- In the story, the people of Ayodhya lit lamps to welcome him.
- On Dhanteras, two days earlier, my parents buy a small steel pot.
- My brother and I make a rangoli with rice flour and petals.
- At night we light diyas on every windowsill.
- My grandparents give us blessings and a little shagun money.
- Diwali teaches me to be kind and to share.

### 5. Class 3 (ages 8–9): about 12 words a line, with a question

NCERT expects Class 3 to use question marks, full stops and capitals. Line 8 asks a question; line 10 exclaims.

- Diwali, or Deepavali, is a five-day festival that ends with Bhai Dooj.
- The main night is Amavasya, when the moon cannot be seen.
- In 2027, Dhanteras is on 27 October and Lakshmi Puja on 29 October.
- On Choti Diwali, people remember Lord Krishna defeating the demon Narakasura.
- Our family places a row of diyas along the balcony railing.
- My aunt makes besan laddoos, and I am allowed to roll them.
- After the puja, we visit three neighbours with homemade sweets.
- Did you know the day after Diwali is New Year for many Gujarati families?
- We keep a bucket of water near the lamps to stay safe.
- Diwali is my favourite festival because the whole family is home!

### 6. Class 4 (ages 9–10): about 13 words a line, linked in order

NCERT's Class 4 outcomes include 7–8 sentence dictation and linkers such as "First" and "Next". This set uses them across the five days.

- Diwali is celebrated in India and by Indian families in many other countries.
- It usually comes in October or November, and schools close for a few days.
- First, families clean their homes, because a tidy home is said to welcome Lakshmi.
- Next, on Dhanteras, many people buy something made of metal, such as a spoon.
- On Lakshmi Puja, the third day, families pray for good fortune after sunset.
- In 2027 that puja falls on Friday, 29 October, and Govardhan Puja follows.
- Govardhan Puja recalls Krishna lifting a hill to shelter villagers from rain.
- The festival ends with Bhai Dooj, when sisters pray for their brothers' long lives.
- In West Bengal, many families worship Goddess Kali at this time of year.
- My favourite part is lighting the first diya with my grandfather.

### 7. Class 5 (ages 10–11): about 14 words a line, with facts you can check

Line 2 rests on [UNESCO's 2025 inscription of Deepavali](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/deepavali-02312), and line 4 on [Drik Panchang's 2027 Lakshmi Puja timings](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/lakshmipuja/festivals-lakshmipuja-timings.html?year=2027) for New Delhi, checked 22 October 2026. Drik Panchang lists Tamil Deepavali a day earlier, on 28 October 2027, so Tamil Nadu pupils should check the school calendar.

- Deepavali is a festival of lamps celebrated across India, and Diwali is its shorter name.
- In 2025, UNESCO added Deepavali to its list of the world's intangible cultural heritage.
- It follows the moon, so the date moves: 8 November in 2026, 29 October in 2027.
- According to Drik Panchang, the new-moon tithi ends at 7:05 pm on 29 October 2027.
- The north recalls Rama's return to Ayodhya; parts of the south, Krishna's victory over Narakasura.
- In Tamil Nadu, many families begin Deepavali with an oil bath before sunrise.
- Gujarati traders open fresh account books at Diwali, and their New Year follows.
- Our school asks us to celebrate with clay diyas and rangoli instead of loud crackers.
- This year my cousin and I will make a rangoli of 51 dots.
- To me, Diwali means thanking everyone who helped us all year.

## Words per line by class, against NCERT's 2017 writing goals

This table compares five age bands by line length, NCERT's outcome and dated facts. Below Class 3, ten written lines exceed NCERT's goal, so a younger child can say five and copy five.

| Set on this page | Average words per line | NCERT 2017 writing outcome | Dated facts in the set |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nursery, LKG and UKG | 5–6 | Class 1: writes simple words such as "fan", "hen", "rat" | 0 |
| Classes 1 and 2 | 8–10 | Class 2: composes and writes simple, short sentences | 1 (29 October 2027) |
| Class 3 | 12 | 5–6 sentences on personal experiences; uses ?, full stops, capitals | 2 |
| Class 4 | 13 | Dictation of 7–8 sentence paragraphs; linkers "First", "Next" | 1 |
| Class 5 | 14 | Paragraphs with punctuation and linkers | 4 |

## Helping a child turn these sets into their own 10 lines

Talk first, then write. A [2024 PLOS ONE study of 191 Spanish-speaking children](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12140084) found that kindergarten storytelling skill predicted sentence complexity in Grade 1, while handwriting and spelling mostly predicted how much they wrote (abstract read).

So ask the child to tell you about their Diwali in ten spoken sentences. Then take one line from their class set and swap a detail, such as their own rangoli's colours. Finally, join two short lines with "because" and swap a repeated name for "he" or "she".

## Where SubhSandesh fits, and where it does not

SubhSandesh is not an essay tool and writes no homework. Its Diwali page is a greeting for one person, useful once the lines exist and a child wants to send a few to a grandparent far away.

On [SubhSandesh's interactive Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali), a parent can type three of the child's lines as wishes on a row of diyas and add up to six family photos to the sky lanterns. It takes about 5 minutes and opens in any browser with no app, which matters when 48.3% of shared pages open on a phone. Do it the evening before: in Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest festival analogue (n = 89), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself.

If the child wrote all ten lines, [the photo jigsaw template](https://subhsandesh.in/photo-puzzle) fits better: each piece placed reveals one line of a letter. It is not a Diwali template; the words carry the festival.

It is the wrong choice for homework, which schools want handwritten. For a grandparent in the same house, a handwritten card beats any link, however often it is reopened (11.1 views per page).

## Sources

- NCERT, *Learning Outcomes at the Elementary Stage*, April 2017.
- NCERT, *National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage*, 20 October 2022.
- Jiménez and colleagues, *PLOS ONE* 19(12): e0315748, 27 December 2024 (abstract read).
- UNESCO, *Deepavali*, inscribed 2025.
- Drik Panchang, *Lakshmi Puja 2027*: date reference, undated.
